The param string (query[1]) is extracted from the user-supplied outer query by extract_query_params() (regex `param_query_(\d+)_{([^}]+)}`), passed as `params` to get_query_results(), and replace_query_parameters() does `query_text.replace('{{{key}}}', value[0])` — a plain str.replace with no binding, escaping, or allowlist. The resulting query_text is executed by `query.data_source.query_runner.run_query(query_text, user)` (line 76), a raw-SQL API. Unlike the established handler path (redash/handlers/query_results.py:263-283), which refuses to run queries with text parameters under view-only access via `query.parameterized.is_safe` (redash/models/parameterized_query.py:174-176), this new runner path only checks `has_access(query.data_source, user, view_only)` (line 51) and never applies the is_safe guard, so a view-only user can inject arbitrary SQL into the sub-query. The param string is also attacker-controlled (it is part of the outer query text the caller supplies), so the injected value is fully attacker-influenced.

findings.suggested_fix: Do not build SQL by string-replacing parameter values into the query text. Either (a) pass the sub-query through the same ParameterizedQuery.apply() path used by redash/handlers/query_results.py so values are validated against the parameter schema and the is_safe guard is enforced (refuse to run text-parameterized queries under view-only access), or (b) bind the parameter values as bound parameters in the sub-query instead of concatenating them, and validate/allowlist the parameter names. At minimum, apply the `query.parameterized.is_safe` check in _load_query/get_query_results before executing a parameterized sub-query, mirroring the established handler pattern.

Because the substituted value is concatenated into the SQL text rather than passed as a bound parameter, an attacker who can supply the parameter value (e.g. via the results API endpoint that takes parameter values) can inject arbitrary SQL. This code path is new in the PR (base get_query_results had no params argument and no replace_query_parameters).

findings.suggested_fix: Do not substitute parameter values into the SQL text via string replacement. Instead, pass the parameter values as bound parameters to the underlying query runner (e.g. use the data source's parameterized query support / placeholders), or validate/escape the values against the target dialect before interpolation. Never concatenate attacker-controlled values into executable SQL text.

- We added server side validation of parameter values for all parameter types, except for parameters of `text` type. All validated parameter types are considered safe. When a query is using safe parameters (or no parameters at all), View Only users can refresh it.
- Refreshing safe queries is done using the new results API endpoint, which takes only a query ID (and optionally parameter values) and does not need the query text.

### Query Editor Improvements

- Run only the highlighted query text: hit Execute after highlighting a portion of your query and only the selected portion will be sent to the database. This is useful for testing sub-SELECT statements and CTE's.
- Improved auto complete: add a dot . after a table name in the query editor and auto complete will only suggest columns on that table.
- Autosave parameter configuration changes.
- YAML syntax support (for data sources like Yandex Metrica).

### Improved Query Scheduler

The Query Scheduler got a face lift and some new options: you can pick a day for a weekly schedule to run on and also set an end date after which the query will no longer execute on schedule.

### Data Sources

We added Apache Drill, Uptycs and a new JSON data source. Also fixed a few bugs in Athena's query runner and others.

### User Management

The users page got revamped with a new look and feel and few new features:

- An indication when a user was last active.
- Show if an invited user hasn't finished the setup process yet (Pending Invitations section).
- You can now generate a new API key for users, if there's a concern it was compromised.

### Admin

- New Celery queues status screens, replacing the old Queries Status and better reflecting the status of running queries.
- Make the queue name for schema refresh job configurable. The default used to be hard coded `schemas`, which is not available on all setups. Now it's `celery`.
- The `gevent` library is installed by default, and you can now setup gunicorn to use `gevent` based workers.
